T-001.Title: Enforce context.read and text.edit on /ext/context and /ext/apply and name the granted capabilities in the pairing dialog

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Introduce the RouteCapability permission-class enum in src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs inside START_BLOCK_AUTH_EXTRACT (after validate_bearer, before authenticate_incoming): a private Copy enum with exactly four variants StreamDocument, ContextRead, TextEdit, TextInsert, a name() mapping to "stream.document", "context.read", "text.edit", "text.insert" respectively, a grant_phrase() mapping to "send streamed documents to Mark for display", "read the current text of the active tab", "edit the current text of the active tab", "insert text at the active tab cursor" respectively, and an all() fixed order [StreamDocument, ContextRead, TextEdit, TextInsert] for deterministic dialog listing. Change authenticate_incoming's capability parameter from Option<&str> to Option<RouteCapability>, with the candidate selection using capability.map(|cap| registry.get_enabled(cap.name())) and the manifest check at line 451 using capability.is_none_or(|cap| manifest.capabilities.iter().any(|c| c.name == cap.name())); update its doc comment to describe every incoming data route instead of text insertion only. Rewire the three call sites: handle_text_insert line 988 passes Some(RouteCapability::TextInsert) (behavior identical), handle_ext_context line 1039 passes Some(&req.extension_id), Some(RouteCapability::ContextRead) and handle_ext_apply line 1117 passes Some(&req.extension_id), Some(RouteCapability::TextEdit), so an enabled token-valid extension whose registered manifest lacks the route's capability is refused with 401 UNAUTHORIZED through the existing BLOCK_AUTH_FAILED_INCOMING path before any content is returned or any mt::text::op or context event is emitted. The stream routes keep exactly their C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH fencing — no manifest capability check is added to or removed from /stream/open, /stream/patch, /stream/close or /stream/heartbeat, and token issuance, keychain storage, pairing approval flow and disable/revocation semantics are untouched.

Rework the release pairing dialog in handle_pair to state the exact grant: change State(_state) to State(state), look up the registered manifest for req.extension_id through state.app_handle.state::<ExtRegistry>().get_manifest before the spawn_blocking dialog closure, and build the description through a new pure pub(super) helper pairing_grant_description(extension_name, extension_id, declared_capability_names) that lists, in RouteCapability::all() fixed order and only for capabilities the manifest actually declares, one "- {grant_phrase}" line each, falls back to the single honest line "- pair with Mark (its manifest declares no incoming data routes yet)" when nothing incoming-route-relevant is declared or no manifest is registered, and composes "The extension "{name}" ({id}) wants to pair with Mark.

If you allow pairing, it will be able to:
{lines}Anything not listed here is not granted to this extension." — the old sentence "Allow this extension to send documents and data to Mark?" is removed. Keep the cfg(not(debug_assertions)) gating, rfd MessageDialog shape, Info level, Allow/Deny OkCancelCustom buttons, spawn_blocking wrapper and unwrap_or(false) fallback, and the debug-build auto-approval arm byte-identical; keep the helper compiled in debug builds with a cfg_attr(debug_assertions, allow(dead_code)) so the pure description is unit-testable. The helper never claims tab read or edit access for a stream-only manifest.

T-002.Title: Flip the over-grant pin to per-route denial, pin the read/edit permission matrix, and prove the refusal red-before green-after

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first proof, recorded in the task evidence: with the new tests authored, temporarily restore the two T-001 call sites to capability None, run the renamed pin and the two matrix tests and observe them fail exactly on the over-grant refusals (context/apply answering 200 for a stream-only fixture), then restore Some(RouteCapability::ContextRead)/Some(RouteCapability::TextEdit) and observe the same tests pass; this is the spec's over-grant-regression fails-before-passes-after criterion exercised inside one worktree without any commit.

Rewrite the pinned over-grant regression in src-tauri/src/m045_ext/tests.rs START_BLOCK_DISABLE_AUTH_TESTS: enabled_extension_passes_all_three_routes becomes enabled_extension_passes_only_declared_capability_routes asserting for the text.insert fixture (context 401, apply 401, insert 200 with exactly one mt::text::op event) and for the stream.document fixture (context 401, apply 401 with zero mt::text::op events, insert 401, and stream_open_fixture stays 200 OK for the same token — the owned stream route keeps working). Add the permission-matrix cases in START_BLOCK_INCOMING_DATA_TESTS: context_requires_context_read_capability (a context.read fixture gets context 200 while apply and insert are 401; a text.edit fixture gets context 401) and apply_requires_text_edit_capability (a text.edit fixture gets apply 200 emitting exactly one insert mt::text::op for the insert_at_cursor operation while context and insert are 401; a context.read fixture gets apply 401 with zero events). Every refusal asserts the empty event list so no mt::text::op is emitted without the matching grant.

Add the dialog-grant unit pin (compiled debug too, since pairing_grant_description is pub(super) and pure): pairing_grant_description_names_only_declared_capabilities asserts that a stream.document-only declaration yields a description containing the stream phrase and neither "read the current text of the active tab" nor "edit the current text of the active tab", that a context.read-plus-text.edit declaration names exactly those two phrases in fixed order, and that an empty or unknown declaration list falls back to the "declares no incoming data routes" line — expectations stated independently from the implementation strings.

Reconcile the disable/pairing family with the new matrix without weakening any fencing expectation: fresh_pairing_restores_access switches to a text.edit fixture (fresh pairing restores apply 200 and insert 200 while context stays 401) plus a context.read fixture (fresh pairing restores context 200 while apply and insert stay 401); assert_old_token_fenced keeps all three routes 401 for old tokens; disable_revokes_and_verifies_absence, disable_surfaces_revoke_failure and disable_refuses_unverified_revocation keep their text.insert fixtures and assertions unchanged; the text_insert_* family and the stream security family stay untouched and green; no existing expectation is weakened or deleted, only capability declarations and the refusals they now imply change.
